nodes.text: Come stand by the fire — the Ring leaves a chill in new folk that takes half a day to shake. I'm *Iona*. I keep this hearth, and the first thing every waker learns at it is the same: the road runs on food, not courage.

Easiest meal in the valley: the *berry banks* along the brook, just east of here. Walk up to a bush and pick it clean — it'll grow back before you miss it. Berries in your pocket mean a bad day is only ever a bad hour.

Now the proper lesson. Take these — {item:raw_chicken} — and put them to my fire. Stand at the flames and cook; the bird will tell you when it's done. A cooked meal heals better than a raw hope, and every campfire in the world works like this one. Learn it here, use it everywhere.
And if you scorch the first one — good. Everyone does. _The fire keeps the first bird as tuition._ The second one you'll eat. Off you go, and come see me whenever the pot's on.
Anything else before your fingers thaw?

East, toward the brook — you'll see the bushes heavy along the near bank, south of the bridge. Fibre plants and sageroot grow wild there too; Fen has uses for the one, and any herbalist you ever meet will bless you for the other. Pick what you pass.
Eat before you train and sleep before you travel. That's the whole of hearth-wisdom, free of charge.
